title: SmoothQuant scaling plus residual Mirror rotation
hypothesis: After a SmoothQuant-style diagonal scale, a residual block-Hadamard rotation can improve held-out int4 reconstruction over either component alone at a small actual byte and compute cost.
physical_object: 12 Pythia-70M attention-dense and MLP-up matrices in layers 0-5, width 512
mirror_coordinate: Per-matrix selection among 16 exact block-Hadamard/sign/permutation gauges applied after SmoothQuant scaling
logical_multiplicity: Alternative residual quantization gauges of a single shared weight set; no functional capacity claim

split.evaluation_units: output rows of each of 12 matrices
split.global_code_fit: calibration rows across all matrices; no audit rows used

quantization.smooth_scale: FP16 per input channel; derived from calibration output rows only

development.selection_metric: mean audit-row relative Frobenius NRMSE across all 12 matrices, actual total/code/scale bytes, elapsed calibration/encode and operation proxies

controls: QuaRot residual only with one shared selected code
SmoothQuant plus one shared residual code
SmoothQuant plus per-matrix best-of-16 residual code

paid_objects: all selected rotation sign/permutation arrays and IDs

success_gate: Both dev seeds: SmoothQuant+residual rotation improves held-out NRMSE by >=2% versus SmoothQuant alone and >=1% versus rotation alone; total serialized payload <=1.01x the best single component; no exact native sequential alias.
failure_gate: Any quality or byte gate miss, or exact native sequential SmoothQuant+QuaRot alias.
boundaries: Small Pythia weight-matrix reconstruction screen; output-row audit, not held-out layer generalization
Natural-text task quality and full-model inference remain untested
Fresh remains sealed after any development gate miss or exact native alias
